title: "Hands-On: A Pre-Commit Hook"
---

# Hands-On: Create a Pre-Commit Hook

Install a `pre-commit` that runs `git diff --cached --check` on `desk-api`.

```bash
cd ~/desk/desk-api

cat > .git/hooks/pre-commit <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
echo "pre-commit: git diff --cached --check" >&2
git diff --cached --check
EOF
chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
test -x .git/hooks/pre-commit
```

## Fail on purpose

```bash
printf 'trailing space \n' >> README.md
git add README.md
git commit -m "docs: should fail the hook"
```

Expect a non-zero exit and no new commit. `git log -1 --oneline` is unchanged.

## Pass

```bash
git restore --staged README.md
git restore README.md
echo "hooks lab" >> README.md
git add README.md
git commit -m "docs: hooks lab"
git status
```

Clean status, new commit. Remove the hook when you are done with the lab, or leave it — `--check` is a good default:

```bash
rm -f .git/hooks/pre-commit
```

Leave it in place if you want the check on this clone.
